description: Surviving mutants documented as equivalent: no input makes the mutated program observably differ from the original at its public interface. Each rule names the mutation operators and a source-text pattern (so it survives line renumbering) and the reason. scripts/mutation-summary.ts reports the score with and without them; the raw score, which the break threshold uses, is never adjusted. See docs/CONFORMANCE-COVERAGE.md.

rules.reason: The message of an internal exception. Every such exception is caught by the enclosing try/catch and mapped to a fixed decision; the text is never observed.

rules.linePattern: height\.set\(name, h\)|path\.add\(name\)|if \(path\.has\(name\)\) throw|if \(known !== undefined\) return known|visiting\.add\(|done\.add\(k\.id\)|if \(done\.has\(k\.id\)\) return true|if \(!admitted\.has\(c\.id\)\)
rules.reason: Memoization and cycle bookkeeping. Without the memo the traversal recomputes the same value; without the in-progress marker a cycle recurses until the stack overflows, which the enclosing try/catch turns into the same fail-closed result (null or false) as the explicit cycle check.

rules.linePattern: depth >= LIMITS\.path \|\| visiting\.has\(resource\.id\)|completed\.has\(resource\.id\)\) return depth|visit\(source, depth \+ 1\)\) return false|completed\.set\(resource\.id, height\); return depth
rules.reason: Redundant depth accounting in visible(). The height of the whole graph is computed bottom-up and compared at the root (depth 0 + height <= LIMITS.path), so the entry check, the memoized-path check and the per-node check only end the traversal earlier; a cycle yields an undefined height (NaN) that fails the comparison at the root.

rules.linePattern: child\.id !== parent\.id|child\.tenant === parent\.tenant|child\.subject === parent\.subject|!!agent && agent\.tenant === child\.tenant|agent\.kind === 'agent' && agent\.active
rules.reason: canDelegate() repeats conditions that grantValid(next, child) checks again through the child's own chain (tenant, subject, agent liveness and tenant; a grant that is its own parent is a cycle).

In lineageLive() every edge leads to a visit that increments the node count first, so the 1024-node budget is exhausted before the 4096-edge budget can be; a null reference throws and is caught as false, like an invalid id (see the findings).
A null source reference throws inside a try/catch that returns the same fail-closed value as the identifier check.

rules.linePattern: limit: number = LEVELS\.length - 1, open = false|let limit = LEVELS\.length - 1;|options\.risk === false \? LEVELS\.length - 1
rules.reason: A default that the callers always override, or an upper bound that the clearance index or the first cap of the loop already lowers.

rules.linePattern: activeRoles\.length > LIMITS\.roles|activeRoles\.some\(r => typeof r !== 'string' \|\| !r\)|typeof r === 'string' && held\.has\(r\)
rules.reason: grantValid() and sessionRoles() both reject an activation that is not a list of held role names, and held.has() is false for anything that is not a string; the second check is the one that decides.

rules.linePattern: parent\.maxResults === undefined \|\| \(grant\.maxResults !== undefined|parent\.heartbeatTtlMs === undefined \|\| \(grant\.heartbeatTtlMs !== undefined|parent\.tenant === grant\.tenant
rules.reason: An undefined child value compared with a number is NaN and fails the comparison anyway; the tenant of a parent is checked again through the parent's own subject.

risky only selects the reason (RISK_CAP or KNOWLEDGE_BOUNDARY) of a denial that visible() already decided, and a principal whose cap is below public is denied with RISK_CAP by the fallback path as well; neither changes an effect.
A missing destination record throws on the next property access and is caught as a denial; a non-string id never names a record (Object.hasOwn coerces it to a key that no record has).

rules.linePattern: const plain = |const only = |&& prior\.type === o\.type|LEVELS\.indexOf\(o\.value\) > LEVELS\.indexOf\(prior\.value\)|if \(o\.type === 'runtime_profile'\) \{|list\.some\(p => p\.type === 'runtime_profile'|typeof x === 'string' && /\^
rules.reason: Type tests that the following conjunct already implies (a primitive has no `type`; a missing required member fails the value check; the prior obligation was looked up by its own type); equal levels assign the same value; identifier and trace-id tests fail for non-strings through the regular expression.

Comparator boundary for equal ids (ids are unique, so equality never occurs) and the second ternary of a sort comparator, which only tells 0 from 1: the engine's sort acts on negative results only. The first ternary is pinned by tests with unsorted input.
The outer loop only skips the remaining work after a bound was already reported; the returned records and the flag are unchanged.
Entries of other obligation types are keyed by an undefined domain and never read back; the merged map only holds runtime_profile entries.
When the chain is null the function returns null on the next line whatever the levels are.

rules.linePattern: const index = cap === 'deny' \? -1 : LEVELS\.indexOf\(cap as Level\)
rules.reason: LEVELS.indexOf('deny') is -1 as well: the cap denies either way.

rules.linePattern: grant\.breakGlass === true && grant\.parent === undefined|grant\.breakGlass === undefined && parent\.breakGlass === undefined|if \(!label \|\| !Array\.isArray\(k\.sources\)\) throw|chain\.some\(c => c\.id === id\)|if \(!held\) return false;
rules.reason: Conditions that a second check subsumes: a break-glass grant with a parent is rejected by breakGlassShape() and by the delegation clause alike; sources that are not a list throw in the loop and are caught; a container cycle also hits the depth bound; missing roles throw in audience() and are caught.

The subject of a grant in a chain is the evaluated user, whose existence, activity and tenant decide() has checked; a missing agent would throw and be caught, and the vectors pin the unknown-agent case as INVALID_DELEGATION.
A primitive record has no tenant and is filtered out by the tenant comparison anyway.
